Detailed View of MicroStrategy (MSTR) Options Chain Expiring 2026-10-09

A complete, real‑time snapshot of MicroStrategy (MSTR) equity options expiring on 2026‑10‑09 is now available. The page lists every call and put contract for the single expiration date, showing pricing, liquidity, and volatility metrics.

🔍 Overview

  • The chain displays each contract’s symbol, last trade price, bid/ask quotes, daily change, % change, trading volume, open interest, implied volatility (IV), and in‑the‑money (ITM) status.
  • Traders use a specific expiry’s options chain to identify key strike levels, unusual activity, and risk‑hedging behavior.
  • High open interest or sudden spikes in volume can reveal where large traders and market makers are concentrating positions.

📈 How Traders Use the Data

  • Compare strike prices, pricing, liquidity (volume & open interest), and IV to spot popular strike zones.
  • Identify where the market is positioning ahead of the expiration by observing changes in volume, open interest distribution, and IV across calls and puts.
  • Use high open‑interest strikes as potential support/resistance levels and as indicators of large‑trader concentration.
  • Monitor sudden volume spikes to detect unusual activity that may precede price moves.

⚙️ Key Metrics Explained

  • Last Trade – most recent transaction price for the option.
  • Bid/Ask – best buying (bid) and selling (ask) prices offered.
  • Volume – number of contracts traded during the current session.
  • Open Interest – total contracts outstanding that have not been exercised or closed.
  • Implied Volatility (IV) – market‑expected volatility of the underlying stock, expressed as a percentage.
  • ITM (In‑The‑Money) – indicates whether the option’s strike price is favorable relative to the current underlying price.

The chain provides a strike‑by‑strike breakdown of pricing, liquidity, and volatility, enabling traders to build a complete view of positioning and risk for MSTR on the 2026‑10‑09 expiration.
